slides.title: 5 reasons you're [[irritable]] 3 weeks after quitting p*rn.
slides.sub: Short fuse on Day 21? Many people say the same.

slides.title: Reasons [[1–2]]
items: Your old escape is gone. Stress has nowhere to hide now.
Feelings come back. P*rn was numbing more than you knew.

slides.title: Reasons [[3–4]]
items: Your sleep is shifting. Late-night routines changed.
Urges are tiring. Saying no all day wears you down.

slides.title: You're [[feeling]] things
slides.body: Irritable isn't failing. It's life without p*rn turning the volume down. Many people say it eases with time.

slides.title: Take the [[edge]] off

Talk it out before it builds up.

carousels.name: 4 reasons you keep searching for something new in p*rn (39B searches)

slides.title: 4 reasons you keep searching for [[something new]] in p*rn.
slides.sub: 39 billion searches in one year. You're not the only one hunting.

slides.title: Searches in [[one year]]
slides.body: P*rnhub alone recorded 39 billion searches in 2019, according to its own Year in Review. That's a lot of people looking for "the next one."

slides.title: Reasons [[1–2]]
items: Novelty is the hook. New content gives a bigger rush than repeats.
The rush fades fast, so you search for the next one.

slides.title: Reasons [[3–4]]
items: Tolerance builds. What worked last month feels flat now.
The search becomes the habit — sometimes more than the p*rn itself.

slides.title: Break the [[hunt]]
items: Notice the search — that's the urge, not the content.
Close the tab the moment you start scrolling for "better".
Block search terms on your devices.
Remind yourself: the next one won't be different.

slides.sub: Two days off. Where did they go?

items: Saturday morning starts in bed with your phone.
"Just one video" turns into the whole afternoon.
You cancel plans to stay in with p*rn.

slides.title: Ways [[4–6]]
items: Sunday comes with guilt, not rest.
Nothing got done — not the gym, not the project, not the call.
Monday starts tired, and the cycle restarts.

carousels.name: 4 kinds of friends who make quitting p*rn harder

slides.title: 4 kinds of friends who make [[quitting p*rn harder.]]
slides.sub: Not bad people. Just bad for your recovery.

slides.title: The [[joker]]
slides.body: Laughs off p*rn addiction and turns your quitting into a running joke. Hard to stay serious when everyone's laughing.

slides.title: The [[sharer]]
slides.body: Sends suggestive memes and clips "for fun." One message can undo a good week without p*rn.

slides.title: Types [[3–4]]
items: The enabler: "One time won't hurt, bro."
The late-night friend: always online, always keeping you up.

slides.title: What to [[do]]
items: Tell them plainly you're quitting p*rn — no apology.
Mute the chats that keep sending triggers.
Spend more time with friends who build you up.
Find one friend who's quitting too.
